title: Slicing Aided Hyper Inference and Fine-tuning for Small Object Detection

problem.summary: Small objects and objects far away in the scene are a major challenge in surveillance and aerial imaging: they occupy few pixels, lack detail, and cause detectors trained on standard low-resolution datasets with large objects to lose accuracy on high-resolution drone and surveillance imagery, while high-resolution inputs also raise memory requirements.
statements: Small and distant objects are represented by few pixels and lack sufficient details, making them difficult to detect with conventional detectors.
Detectors trained on standard datasets yield significantly lower accuracy on small object detection in high-resolution drone and surveillance images.
DORI criteria require 10% of image height to detect an object, a pixel coverage many real-world objects do not meet.
Prior small-object methods require training from scratch, segmentation annotations, or detector-specific implementations, so they are not generic or fine-tunable.

evidence.quote: Detection of small objects and objects far away in the scene is a major challenge in surveillance applications.
Such objects are represented by small number of pixels in the image and lack sufficient details, making them difficult to detect using conventional detectors.
they yield significantly lower accuracy on small object detection tasks in high-resolution images generated by the high-end drone and surveillance cameras.

background.summary: The work situates itself among single-stage detectors (SSD, YOLO, RetinaNet, FCOS, VFNet, TOOD) and two-stage proposal methods (Fast/Faster/Cascade R-CNN), and against prior small-object remedies (PSO/BFO-trained detectors, copy-paste augmentation, enlarged-region features, attention-based cropping, windowed satellite detection), claiming the gap is that none is a generic slicing pipeline that layers on top of any pretrained detector.

relatedWork.name: Faster R-CNN
relatedWork.relation: representative two-stage region-proposal baseline for general detection
relatedWork.quote: region proposal based methods, such as Fast R-CNN [11], Faster R-CNN [1], Cascade R-CNN [3], involve an initial region proposal stage.

relatedWork.name: FCOS
relatedWork.relation: anchor-free one-stage detector used as an experimental baseline
relatedWork.quote: FCOS [13] is the first object detector eliminating the need for predefined set of anchor boxes and entailing computational need.

relatedWork.name: Windowed networks (Van Etten)
relatedWork.relation: prior slicing-based technique, but not generic across detectors
relatedWork.quote: In [19], a slicing based technique is proposed but the implementation is not generic and only applicable to specific object detectors.

relatedWork.name: PSO/BFO-based learning strategy
relatedWork.relation: prior small-object remedy whose heavy modifications block fine-tuning from pretrained weights
relatedWork.quote: However, these heavy modifications to the original models prevent fine-tuning from pretrained weights and require training from scratch.

evidence.quote: These datasets mostly involve low-resolution images (640 × 480) including considerably large objects with large pixel coverage (covering 60% of the image height in average).
The algorithms designed for general object detection perform poorly on high resolution images that contain small and dense objects, leading to specific approaches for small object detection.

solution.summary: SAHI provides a detector-agnostic pipeline: during slicing aided fine-tuning the training set is augmented with overlapping image patches resized larger so relative object sizes grow, and during slicing aided hyper inference the query image is cut into overlapping patches that are each run through the detector (optionally together with full-image inference), with predictions merged back into original coordinates via NMS.
solution.approach: Slice high-resolution images into overlapping patches, run the detector per patch (and optionally on the full image), then merge the predictions with NMS in original coordinates.
components: overlapping M x N patch slicing with hyper-parameter size ranges
optional full-inference (FI) on the original image for large objects
NMS merging with match threshold Tm and detection threshold Td
slicing aided fine-tuning (SF) dataset augmentation with patches plus original images

evidence.quote: an open-source framework called Slicing Aided Hyper Inference (SAHI) is proposed that provides a generic slicing aided inference and finetuning pipeline for small object detection.
The proposed technique is generic in the sense that it can be applied on top of any available object detector without any fine-tuning.
Dividing the input images into overlapping patches results in relative larger pixel areas for small objects with respect to the images fed into the network.
Finally, the overlapping prediction results and, if used, FI results are merged back into to original size using NMS.

experiments.summary: Integrated into FCOS, VFNet and TOOD via MMDetection and evaluated with the COCO AP50 protocol on VisDrone2019-Detection test-dev and the xView validation split, ablating slicing aided fine-tuning (SF), sliced inference (SAHI), full-image inference (FI) and 25% patch overlap (PO), plus TIDE-style error analysis.

evidence.quote: the proposed inference method can increase object detection AP by 6.8%, 5.1% and 5.3% for FCOS, VFNet and TOOD detectors, respectively.
resulting in a cumulative increase of 12.7%, 13.4% and 14.5% AP in the same order.
Since xView targets are very small, regular training with original images yields poor detection performance and SF improves the results substantially.
Best small object detection AP is achieved by SF followed by SI, while best large object detection AP is achieved by SF followed by FI, confirming the contribution of FI for large object detection.

limitations.summary: There is no dedicated limitations section; the authors note that smaller patches can exclude larger objects, sliced inference increases computation linearly, error analysis leaves major room on false positives and negatives, and all reported numbers use a single AP50 IoU threshold.
items: As patch sizes decrease, larger objects may not fit within a slice, harming detection of large objects.
Sliced inference increases computational time linearly (though memory stays fixed).
Error analysis shows major remaining room on false positives and false negatives.
Adding full-image inference raises large-object AP but slightly decreases small/medium AP.
Evaluation is limited to AP50 at a single IoU threshold of 0.5.

evidence.quote: as the patch sizes decrease, larger objects may not fit within a slice and the intersecting areas, and this may lead to poor detection performance for larger objects.
The proposed approach increases the computational time linearly, while keeping memory requirements fixed.
major room for improving false positives and false negatives
AP50 is computed at the single IoU threshold 0.5 over all categories and maximum number of detections is set as 500.

futureDirections.direction: Benchmark instance segmentation models with the slicing approach and evaluate alternative post-processing techniques.
futureDirections.quote: In the future, instance segmentation models will be benchmarked utilizing the proposed slicing approach and different post-processing techniques will be evaluated.

equations.name: Patch slicing grid
equations.expr: image I sliced into l overlapping M x N patches with M in [Mmin, Mmax], N in [Nmin, Nmax] treated as hyper-parameters

equations.name: Sliced-inference NMS merge
equations.expr: boxes with IoU ratio > Tm are matched; for each match, detections with probability < Td are removed; Tm = 0.5 in experiments

equations.name: Patch resize for fine-tuning
equations.expr: patch resized preserving aspect ratio so image width is in [800, 1333] pixels

applications.detail: The motivating application is long-range surveillance detection under DORI criteria, where objects may cover only 10-20% of image height.
applications.quote: DORI criteria define the minimum pixel height of the objects for different tasks: 10% of the image height is required to detect and 20% to recognize the objects (108 pixels in full HD videos).

applications.detail: Drone and high-end camera imagery is the target regime; the pipeline is designed for aerial datasets such as VisDrone and xView.
applications.quote: The recent advances in drones, 4K cameras and deep learning research have enabled long-range object detection

applications.domain: autonomous driving and general detection applications
applications.detail: The introduction lists face detection, video object detection, video surveillance and self-driving cars as established application areas of object detection.
applications.quote: In recent years, object detection has been extensively studied for different applications including face detection, video object detection, video surveillance, self-driving cars.

deploymentClaims: The scheme drops into any detection inference pipeline without pretraining and gains up to 6.8% AP from inference alone.
Integrated with Detectron2, MMDetection and YOLOv5; open source at https://github.com/obss/sahi.git
Memory requirements stay fixed while compute grows linearly; patch sizes trade off computation and memory per target platform.

evidence.quote: The proposed slicing aided hyper inference scheme can directly be integrated into any object detection inference pipeline and does not require pretraining.
Computation and memory budgets can also be traded-off by adjusting the patch sizes, considering the target platform.
Proposed technique has been integrated with Detectron2, MMDetection and YOLOv5 models and it is publicly available at https://github.com/obss/sahi.git
